headline: Up Your Arsenal's PAL v1.00 reaches 60.90% matched code, up from 58.58%
summary: A day of shared-level batches took Up Your Arsenal's PAL v1.00 from 58.58% to 60.90% matched code by size. Its progress report now counts 13,815 matched functions out of 16,533 for PAL v1.00. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game.
highlights: PAL v1.00 shared-code batches include 83 functions in #107, 48 in #85, 36 in #101 and 26 in #92, alongside smaller level and boot-program batches.
NTSC-U fixes let more existing C link in Vidcomics, Obani Moons and shared Florana code, with further repairs for native level 39 functions (#90, #91, #93, #95, #97, #98, #100, #104, #105).
Two PAL matches from #77 and #83 still lack matching NTSC-U C. Final checks nevertheless rebuilt all 49 PAL levels and all 54 NTSC-U targets to match, using assembly where C is unfinished.
A conflicting camera-table declaration introduced by #94 and #99 was fixed so level 20, the final boss, builds again.
Open #106 proposes 20 NTSC-U-only functions. #108 proposes five PAL Holostar Studios functions and #109 proposes 22 PAL shared-code functions. These have not landed.
#84 adds six PAL v1.00 boot-program functions. Their NTSC-U counterparts remain drafts, and the corresponding front-end copies still use assembly.
